questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place with easy access to nature where i could hike, camp and surf. I wanted to go to a university that had access to the ocean with good marine and ocean courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. The university keeps you updated on deadines and information through emails on your university profil on the website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There are multiple info sessions and campus tours to give you information about the campus and the resources available on campus and events to mingle with other exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Go the the events in the beginning - it is a great place to meet new friends.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
We found housing pretty early. We found it in January through airbnb and signed the lease.
If you are multiple people from your home university it might be easier to find a big house with space for all of you. This is what we did. Otherwise there are facebook pages where a lot of students also post if they are renting out a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find housing. Start searching early and use the facebook pages to find housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You received an email with a timeslot and date for registration and then you received an email and link to a thorough guide on how to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails with reminders and guides on how to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found out quite late that a lot of the marine courses that I wanted to take, could not be taken on the campus in Victoria but only as part of a bigger program in Bamfield and the rest of the marine courses were in the spring. After finding the new classes I wanted, I could get into all my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to sign up for your classes in your given timeslot to make sure to get at spot on the classes you want. 
Sign up for 1 or 2 extra classes if you end up changing your mind or want to try out some different classes the first weeks of class and then decide after trying them out. Most students do this, as you freely can drop courses for the first few weeks of classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took 300-level courses. The level of the courses I took were quite easy, although this really depends on the course and is not the same for every course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You are graded and evaluated throughout the semester. I liked it this way, as you were forced to participate along the way and the load during the exams in the end was therefore much smaller.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AE303 Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques.
ES 361 The Biodiversity of British Columbia.
EOS 350 Understanding the Oceans.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My favourite course was definitely EOS 350: Understanding the Oceans! In general UVic has a really good Earth and Ocean science program and I believe and have heard that many of their other courses in this field are also good at UVic. EOS 350 was both new stuff to me as a biologist because is started with ocean earth science and later a good blend with biology. The whole course was really interesting to me and the workload was not to big. The exams were all open book, take home exams. 

ES 361 The Biodiversity of British Columbia was a quite fluffy course as it is not a science course. The professor is really nice! The lectures were mostly just talk about different species on a fluffy basis. There was some really interesting stuff as well, but it was mostly just scrapping the surface. It is a smaller class(30-40 people I think) with some cool group projects which included data collection through inaturalist outside of class which I enjoyed a lot!

AE303 Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques 
The course load on this one was bigger than I thought. You can tell that this is a university course with deadlines and requirements. There a quite a few assignments and if you have never done much ceramics like I hadn’t, then be prepared to spend maaany hours in the studio outside of class to practice wheeling and to finish assignments. It ended up being my most stressfull course at times, but also a nice place to be able to go anytime of day to work on your projects and zone out.

questions.answer: Groceries were expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were more expensive.
A lot of sweet treats were cheaper than in Copenhagen.
Coffee at cafes was cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are all the clubs you could possibly imagine. They have a club for everything!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Climbing club! It is a great way to meet people and make new friends. 
Camping Shenanigans - camping club that goes on trips - great people!
Surf club - they do fun trips to Tofino (hard to get onto a trip, but keep trying - we found that the trips later in the semester were easier to get a spot on)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore the island - it has so much to offer!
Go hiking and camping! There are so many amazing hikes and mountains on the island. 
Go surfing in Tofino and by Jordan River or Sombrio.
Go see a hockey game.
Go tidepooling (the club: UVic rockhoppers goes sometimes).
Lucky bar on Mondays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It felt quite easy, people are really friendly and very open, even just strangers you meet on the street.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Join some clubs and join some club trips - great place to meet local students.
I met some good friends through the climbing club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is more homelessness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The friendliness and openness of everyone. People are very inclusive. 
The outdoors/nature mindset that everyone has.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you have the possibility to come before and travel a bit - do it!
2. Join a club, go on a club trip
3. Look into the courses, check what others think of the courses(here on mobility) and take a few ekstra courses from the start so you can test them out a little before being stuck with them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get Revolut to avoid the fee normal banks have for every purchase. 
Tips for car rental: the app Turo works well and is cheap. The same with EVO carshare: Get an EVO account early - it takes some time to process your drivers licens, but it is good to have.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and the nature: insane views and hiking/camping trips that I went on with friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Especially early in the semester: Not having the people around me that know me and that I would usually go to when having a hard time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
